title: WTOP Promotes Polymarket Bonus Around Major Sports Matchups
excerpt: WTOP advertises a $25 Polymarket bonus tied to a $10 deposit. Eligibility, withdrawal rules and market risks deserve a closer look.
author: LokkeeVerse
content:
WTOP is promoting a Polymarket offer that it says gives new users $25 in bonuses after a $10 deposit, with its headline highlighting Cowboys–Eagles, NBA games and the World Series. The promotion brings a financial incentive into the conversation around major sporting events. For readers, the central question is not simply the advertised bonus amount, but what conditions govern eligibility, use and withdrawal.

## What the Advertised Bonus Means

According to WTOP, the offer requires new users to register with its promotional code and make a qualifying deposit. A bonus, however, should not automatically be treated as cash that can be withdrawn immediately. Promotional rewards can take different forms, and the distinction between account credit, trading funds and withdrawable money matters when assessing an offer’s actual value.

Readers should check the platform’s current terms for restrictions involving location, age, account verification and previous registration. Other important questions include when the reward is credited, whether it expires and whether additional activity is required before withdrawal. A sports-focused headline does not establish that every reader can access the platform or qualify for the promotion.

## How Sports Prediction Markets Work

Prediction markets generally allow participants to buy and sell contracts tied to whether a specified outcome occurs. In a sports setting, that might involve the result of a game or another defined event. Contract prices reflect trading activity and expectations, but they are not guarantees of what will happen. Participants can lose money when outcomes move against their positions.

These products also require attention to settlement rules: the precise wording of a market determines what counts as a winning outcome. Fees, liquidity and the ability to exit a position can affect the experience. Legal access and consumer protections may differ by jurisdiction, so readers should not assume that prediction markets operate under the same rules as conventional sportsbooks.

Key points to check:

- Whether the advertised bonus remains available and applies to your account.
- What the reward consists of and whether withdrawal conditions apply.
- Whether participation is lawful and permitted where you live.
- How each market resolves, including cancellations or disputed outcomes.
- What funds you could lose independently of the promotional credit.

Readers should watch for the platform’s current offer terms, any changes to eligibility and the settlement language attached to individual sports markets. Those details are more consequential than the headline reward. A promotion can reduce an initial cost, but it does not remove financial risk or make participation necessary to enjoy the games.
